title: Branch spawning from decision points (foundational)
description: Signature original: Whenever the search reaches a fork, such as two plausible query interpretations, the manager spawns a branch per option instead of committing to one. Each branch carries its own query path, budget slice, and the assumption it is testing. Spawning is explicit and logged, so the full exploration tree stays inspectable. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Branch Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Promise-based branch prioritization (foundational)
description: Signature original: Branches are kept in a priority queue ordered by promise score: early result quality times the branch's remaining budget. The manager always works the most promising branch next, which concentrates effort where payoff is likely. Scores update as results come in, so a branch that looked great but fizzles sinks naturally. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import heapq
pq = []
for bid, promise in [('b1', 0.8), ('b2', 0.5), ('b3', 0.9)]:
    heapq.heappush(pq, (-promise, bid))
print('work order:', [heapq.heappop(pq)[1] for _ in range(len(pq))])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Branch Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Branch pruning on diminishing returns (foundational)
description: Signature original: A branch is pruned when its last several steps produced nothing new, measured by novelty of retrieved records. Pruning returns the branch's remaining budget to the pool for redistribution to live branches. Pruned branches are archived with their partial results, not deleted, in case a later discovery revives them. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Branch Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Merge on branch convergence (foundational)
description: Signature original: When two branches start retrieving the same records, measured by overlap of their recent result sets, they are merged into one. Merging avoids paying twice for the same exploration and combines both branches' assumptions into the surviving branch's notes. The merge point is recorded so the tree shows where paths rejoined. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Branch Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Branch accounting and final report (foundational)
description: Signature original: At mission end the manager reports on every branch: spawned, pruned, merged, and the surviving branch's results. The accounting shows where the budget went and which assumptions paid off, which is how the next mission's branching gets smarter. Nothing about the exploration is hidden in the final report. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
